full_details: Heminges let you leave the Worthies at ten minutes to eleven. At Waterson's board you read the second book standing, the same Richard and the same cousin, and you gave in. Two shillings, the dearest book since Golding. You had stood in it four times since March, and this was the standing that bought it. Drayton, at the next board, said there was no laugh in four books. You talked five minutes of home and of sonnets, and you would not give him a number. The ledger took one line, Daniel ij s, and no total. The almanac had Joan's day. You sent nothing. At the desk the new book and the chronicle lay open together.
one_sentence: You read Daniel's second book standing at Paul's, paid two shillings, and at night kept a finger in his book and a finger in the chronicle.
title: Two shillings, and a finger in each book
